newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: LEND LEASE SAYS WESTPAC A MAJOR INVESTMENT.
newsitem.headline: LEND LEASE SAYS WESTPAC A MAJOR INVESTMENT.

text.p: Financial and property services group Lend Lease Corp said on Thursday that its shareholding in Westpac Banking Corp remained a major investment.
The company would not say, however, when asked at a news conference if it would continue to be the owner of 50 million Westpac shares at the end of 1997/98 (July-June).
"Sure it is a major investment for the group," Lend Lease managing director David Higgins said. "It has got significant unrealised profit," Higgins said.
The 50 million shares, representing 2.81 percent of the bank, are valued in the Lend Lease accounts on a cost basis of A$186.0 million but had a market value at June 30 of A$396.0 million.
Lend Lease also owns another 100 million Westpac shares under a forward sale agreement in which it continues to receive all dividends.

The company said on an after-tax basis it received A$20.6 million in Westpac dividends in 1996/97, as well as sale proceeds of A$68.2 million from the sale of 15 million Westpac shares in April 1997 at A$7.00 each and the 100 million ordinary
Lend Lease said earlier that its 1996/97 net profit rose 15 percent to A$322 million from A$280 million. The rise was in line with market expectations.
Its shares were 20 cents higher at A$28.96 at 1.30 p.m. (0330 GMT).
